biography.education: B.B.A. in Finance, University of Texas at Austin
biography.career: Texas State Senator, District 16, Dallas County (2015-2019). Republican candidate for Governor 2022 (lost to Abbott in primary). Co-founder Huffines Communities (DFW real estate developer). Tea Party activist. Self-describes as Rothbardian libertarian-conservative.
biography.primaryResult: Won Republican primary March 3, 2026 with 57%+ in four-way race; avoided runoff. Defeated acting comptroller Kelly Hancock, railroad commissioner Christi Craddick, and Michael Berlanga.
biography.campaignFinance: Self-funded ~$13M ($10M personal loan + $3M from twin brother Phillip)

policyPositions.position: 'DOGE Texas' — expose waste, fraud, abuse; workforce reduction implied; put savings into property tax relief
Slash/eliminate property taxes — signature issue across 2022 Gov race and 2026 Comptroller race
Will administer $1B ESA program; 'ensure it is transparent and empowers parents with no strings attached'
'Eliminate woke DEI from government'; cites forcing shutdown of state-run transgender youth website
'Stand with Trump to secure border; eliminate all taxpayer-funded benefits to illegal aliens including billions educating illegal aliens in schools'
'Complete abolition of abortion; human life deserves legal protection from conception until natural death; supports enforcement of Comstock Act'
'Put God and prayer back in the classroom'
End 'use it or lose it' mentality in government budgeting

votingRecord.conservativeRanking: 4th most conservative senator in 2017 (Rice University Baker Institute)

keyVotes.action: Authored first TX Constitutional Carry bill; voted yes on compromise open carry SB 17 'with heavy heart' — didn't go far enough

keyVotes.notes: 100% pro-life record per Texas Right to Life

interestGroupRatings.rating: Endorsed (credits him as first TX lawmaker to file Constitutional Carry)

endorsements.name: Donald Trump
endorsements.notes: Countered Gov. Abbott's backing of Kelly Hancock

positionConflicts.conflict: Calls for eliminating/slashing property taxes (major source of local school funding) while promising aggressive implementation of $1B ESA/voucher program. Fiscal mechanics not reconciled.

Cites Murray Rothbard as ideological touchstone (libertarian), but positions on abortion (Comstock Act enforcement), religion in public schools, and LGBT ordinance preemption are socially authoritarian rather than libertarian. Framework applies selectively to fiscal/economic issues.

weakAxes: housing/zoning (real estate background but no stated policy)
